subject.title: cron: ghost runs recorded as ok when gateway is down (durationMs < 50ms)

question: Should the cron ghost-run mitigation be a default-on persisted/configurable warning surface, or should maintainers require a narrower log-only or fail/skipped behavior instead?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the proposed fix affects config, run-log/protocol shape, and UI/docs, which AGENTS.md treats as compatibility-sensitive product surface.

options.title: Refresh linked warning PR
options.body: Proceed with the linked PR or a replacement that keeps the warning scoped to main-session next-heartbeat systemEvent handoffs and proves config/protocol compatibility.

options.title: Narrow to log-only warning
options.body: Avoid new config/protocol surface for now and land only a structured gateway log warning for suspicious fast handoffs.

options.title: Change run outcome semantics
options.body: Reframe fast unconfirmed handoffs as skipped or failed instead of warning-only, accepting a larger behavior change for existing cron jobs.

recommendation.title: Refresh linked warning PR
recommendation.body: Proceed with the linked PR or a replacement that keeps the warning scoped to main-session next-heartbeat systemEvent handoffs and proves config/protocol compatibility.

likelyOwner.reason: The central cron dispatch split and current timer ownership evidence point to vincentkoc as the best available routing candidate for this product-shape decision.
